Doctor: Could you please provide more details about your diabetes status, including whether you have been diagnosed with diabetes, the type of diabetes, and how long you have had it? Additionally, have you had any history of infections or cardiovascular conditions? Patient: I was diagnosed with type two diabetes a few years back, and my blood sugars have been running in the two hundreds, which my doctor doesn't like. My last A1C was about ten, so I know it's not well-controlled. I haven't had any major infections or heart issues that I'm aware of. Doctor: Could you describe the location, size, appearance, and any associated symptoms (e.g., pain, drainage, odor) of the foot ulcer? Have you noticed any changes in its appearance over the past year? Patient: It's on the top of my right foot, near the fifth toe, and it's about an inch in size. It's got some yellow stuff in it, and there's been more drainage lately. It doesn't hurt, but I don't feel much in my foot anyway. I've noticed it hasn't been getting better, and it seems to be getting more draining over time. Doctor: Have you had any recent fever, chills, or signs of systemic infection such as malaise or weight loss? Have you had any prior wound cultures or imaging of the foot ulcer? Patient: I haven't had any fever or chills, but I have been feeling more tired lately. As for imaging, I think they did an x-ray before I came in, and it showed no bone infection, if I remember right. I don't think they did a wound culture. Doctor: Could you please describe the depth of the ulcer and whether there is any necrotic tissue present
